ingredients.item: Boneless pork loin chops, 1/2 inch thick

instructions: Grate half of the onion into a small bowl and set it aside.
Shred half of the cabbage and cut the tomatoes into wedges. Divide them among four plates.
In a small bowl, whisk the ponzu, sake and soy sauce.
Pat the chops dry. Cut a few slits through the tissue between the meat and the fat on both sides of each chop, so they stay flat in the pan.
Sprinkle the salt and pepper over both sides of the chops. Dust them with the flour and shake off the extra.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 2 chops and cook for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden. Transfer them to a plate and repeat with the remaining 1 tbsp oil and chops.

You're cooking the pork to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check a chop there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest chop: it's done when the juices run clear and the center is no longer raw.
Pour the sauce and the grated onion into the same skillet and bring it to a boil over medium-high heat. Cook for 2 minutes, then return the chops and spoon the sauce over them for 1 minute.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Slice the chops into bite-size pieces and lay them on the cabbage and tomato. Spoon the extra sauce over the cabbage.
method_notes: Just One Cookbook slits the chops, dusts them with flour, sears them, and finishes them in a pan sauce of ponzu, sake and soy sauce with grated onion, served on shredded cabbage. A second source (a Worcestershire, ketchup and honey sauce with fried garlic chips) is the more Yokkaichi-style version and differs mainly in the sauce. This one follows Just One Cookbook, scaled to four chops.
